title: Easy exam 6
about: Ten single-choice questions on the basics: one concept each, with the classic look-alike options.

`tr` replaces every occurrence, not only the first one.
`tr` replaces each character of the first set with the one in the same position of the second set.
The text is changed: the dashes become underscores.

questions.title: Installing the boot loader
questions.text: Which command installs GRUB on the first disk of the machine?

options.why: `update-grub` regenerates the menu file `grub.cfg`; it does not install the loader on a disk.
It writes the boot loader to the disk; it is done once, not at every boot.
GRUB is not a service: it runs before the kernel, so `systemd` does not exist yet.
`grub.cfg` is the configuration the loader reads, not the loader itself.

questions.title: PID 1
questions.text: Which process has PID 1 on a Linux system?

options.t: The idle process of the kernel, which runs when nothing else can.
options.why: The idle process has PID 0.

options.t: The boot loader, since it is the first program that runs when the machine is switched on.
options.why: The boot loader finishes its work before the kernel starts: it is not a process of the running system.

options.t: The first process of the running system, started by the kernel (usually systemd).
options.why: It is the first process of the running system and the ancestor of all the others.

options.t: The login shell of the first user who connects to the machine.
options.why: A login shell is an ordinary process that gets whatever PID is next.

questions.title: Creating a hard link
questions.text: `orig.txt` exists and `copy.txt` does not. Which command makes `copy.txt` a hard link to `orig.txt`?

options.why: With `-s` it is a symbolic link, not a hard link.
The existing file goes first: this one looks for a file called `copy.txt` and fails.
It creates a second, independent file with its own inode.
Without options `ln` makes a hard link: the new name is another entry for the same inode.

questions.title: The order of redirections
questions.text: Which statement about `ls /nope /etc/hostname > out 2>&1` is TRUE?

options.t: The error message appears on the screen and the listing goes to `out`.
options.why: That is what `2>&1 > out` does, because the order of the redirections matters.

options.t: Both the error message and the listing appear on the screen, and `out` stays empty.
options.why: Both streams are redirected to the file.

options.t: Nothing appears on the screen: both the error message and the listing go to `out`.
options.why: `> out` points stdout at the file and then `2>&1` makes stderr go where stdout goes now.

options.t: The error message goes to a file called `1`.
options.why: With `&` before the number, `2>&1` duplicates a descriptor and does not name a file.

options.t: The five users who have used `sudo` most often.
options.why: Nothing is counted per user; the lines are shown as they are.

options.t: The last five lines of `auth.log`, whether or not they mention `sudo`.
options.why: `grep` runs first, so `tail` only sees the lines that contain `sudo`.

options.t: The five most recent lines of `auth.log` that mention `sudo`.
options.why: `auth.log` records the commands run with `sudo`; `grep` keeps those lines and `tail` the last five.

options.t: The five oldest lines of `auth.log` that mention `sudo`.
options.why: `tail` takes lines from the end of its input, not from the start.

questions.title: Searching the manual
questions.text: Which command does the same search as `apropos network`?

options.why: `whatis` looks up the name of the page only.
It opens the page called `network`, if there is one; it does not search descriptions.
`-k` makes `man` search the descriptions of all the pages for the keyword.
It opens the info page of a tool called `network`; it is not a keyword search.

options.t: `echo $((7*3))` prints `21`, the product of the numbers.
options.why: True: `$(( ))` evaluates the arithmetic.

options.t: `expr 5 + 3` prints `8`, with spaces around the plus.
options.why: True: the spaces around `+` are needed.
False: variables are strings, so `n` becomes the text `4+1`.
True: `bc` is a calculator that reads expressions from stdin.

questions.title: Anchors in a pattern
questions.text: `w` contains the lines `cat`, `cart`, `scatter`, `cut` and `cat5`. Which statement about `grep '^c.t$' w` is TRUE?

options.why: `.` matches exactly one character, and `cart` has two letters between `c` and `t`.
`^` and `$` force the line to start with `c` and end with `t`.
The whole line must be `c`, one character and `t`.

options.t: It prints nothing, because `^` and `$` cannot be used together.
options.why: They can: together they force the pattern to cover the whole line.

options.t: After a command ends, `$?` holds its exit status.
options.why: True.

options.t: A value of 0 means that the last command ended successfully.
options.why: True: any other value means an error.

options.t: `$?` is the PID of the shell that runs the script.
options.why: False: that is `$$`; `$?` is only the exit status of the last command.
True: `ls` fails because `/nope` does not exist.
